cards.question: What is ghost-crm, and what does its repository hold today?
cards.answer: A DOCS-ONLY repo: the imported Skhokho user docs (VuePress) plus a skill library that specifies the Django rebuild.
cards.explanation: No `manage.py` exists anywhere. The only code is `rewrite_links.py` and five read-only diagnostics. The docs are the product spec, the skills are the knowledge transfer. see 01
cards.anchor: A GHOST town: the tourist guide describes every shop in detail, but behind each painted front there is no building yet.
cards.evidence_quote: You are working in a repository that contains **no application code**.

cards.question: Which rule does ghost-crm exist to protect when code and `docs/` disagree?
cards.answer: The docs are the product ground truth: code conforms to `docs/`, NEVER the reverse; a gap gets a ruling first.
cards.explanation: No original team and no running system can be consulted, so `docs/` plus the ruling register is the only arbiter (rule N3). Breaks if undone: code and docs drift with nothing left to settle them. see 03
cards.confusables: Editing `docs/` to match the code (fenced wrong path W7) — the docs change ONLY through a ruling or a reviewed behaviour change, never to follow code.
cards.evidence_quote: **Docs are the product ground truth.** Code conforms to `docs/`; never edit `docs/` to match code

cards.question: ghost-crm · `rewrite_file()`: recite the 7 steps from reading one docs page to the returned `(count, originals)`.
steps: `LINK_RE.subn(repl, text)` -> skhokho.io links flattened to `NEW_URL`, originals collected
build `footer` -> separator, header, one `- [label](url)` line per original
header already present -> `split()` on the exact separator, keep the part before it
`new_text.rstrip() + footer` -> one fresh block at the end of the page
cards.answer: read · flatten + collect · zero-exit · footer · strip old block · append · write if apply
cards.explanation: The old block is dropped AFTER the substitution, so its entries are what feeds `originals` on a re-run. That ordering is why a re-apply is idempotent (see 70) and why the log always shows the full count (see 92).
cards.anchor: A clerk overstamps every old address on a page, notes each old address once on a slip, tears off last year's slip and staples the new slip to the bottom.
cards.evidence_quote: new_text, count = LINK_RE.subn(repl, text)

cards.question: ghost-crm · `rewrite_file`: a page holds the same skhokho.io link twice. Predict `count` and `len(originals)` after the lines below.
cards.code_snippet:
text = "[Docs](https://skhokho.io/a) and [Docs](https://skhokho.io/a)"

def repl(match):
    label, url = match.group(1), match.group(2)
    key = (label, url)
    if key not in seen:
        seen.add(key)
        originals.append(key)
    return f"[{label}]({NEW_URL})"

new_text, count = LINK_RE.subn(repl, text)
cards.answer: `count` is 2 and `originals` holds 1 pair — every match is REPLACED, but a `(label, url)` pair is archived only once.
cards.explanation: (1) `LINK_RE` matches both links. (2) First call: the key is new, so it is added to `seen` and appended. (3) Second call: the key is already in `seen`, nothing is appended. (4) `subn` reports 2 substitutions. see 12

cards.question: ghost-crm · `rewrite_links.py`: predict the result of the call below, given that `/tmp/nope` does not exist.
cards.answer: It stops: `docs directory not found: /tmp/nope` on stderr and exit code 1 — it NEVER falls back to another tree.

cards.question: Why does ghost-crm forbid hand-editing or deleting a References block rather than tidying it up during the rebrand?
cards.answer: The link rewrite ran BEFORE the docs import was committed, so the pre-rewrite docs exist nowhere in git: the blocks are the only surviving record of the original app's routes.
cards.explanation: They are the raw material for the rebuild's URL design (ruling R10 keeps the originals as a legacy mapping). Breaks if undone: the deep links are gone for good, and a hand-edited separator makes the next `--apply` corrupt the page (see 91).
cards.anchor: A demolished house whose only floor plan is a carbon copy stapled to the back of each brochure: scribble on it and no architect can redraw the rooms.
cards.confusables: A grep-and-replace of `skhokho` across `docs/` — it would also rewrite the ARCHIVED URLs; the rebrand stops above the header (see 94).
cards.evidence_quote: the pre-rewrite docs were never committed. They must never be hand-edited.

cards.question: Why does ghost-crm's rebuild plan set `AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'accounts.User'` BEFORE the first `migrate` rather than start on the default `auth.User` and switch later?
cards.answer: The first `migrate` bakes a foreign key to whatever user model exists at that moment; switching afterwards is unsupported without dropping the database. DESIGN TARGET.
cards.explanation: It is the ONLY irreversible decision of the campaign, so it is made in step 1.3 of phase G1. Breaks if undone: `InconsistentMigrationHistory`; the clean fix is to delete `db.sqlite3` and the generated migrations.
cards.anchor: Concrete poured around the first door frame: to change the door afterwards, the whole foundation has to be broken out.
cards.confusables: Migrating on `auth.User`, then editing `django_migrations` (wrong path W1) — history and schema then DISAGREE forever.
cards.evidence_quote: Changing `AUTH_USER_MODEL` mid-project is officially unsupported without dropping the database.

cards.question: Why does ghost-crm's rebuild plan compute row visibility with decorators and scoped managers in `core` rather than store per-object permission rows with django-guardian? Give the verdict and what the alternative must first prove.
cards.answer: Verdict: computed wins. (1) Visibility derives from current FKs (line-manager tree, org-wide HR overlay, creator/assignee), so a reassignment needs ZERO permission writes. (2) Stored rows imply a bulk rewrite of grants on every `line_manager` change; guardian is admissible only with a written derivation of how they stay correct. (3) One engine is provable as the G2 permission matrix; per-view if-statements are wrong path W2. DESIGN TARGET.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: after a change of manager, stale rows keep granting access to former reports. see 22
cards.anchor: A guard who reads the org chart on the wall each time someone knocks, instead of a drawer of keys that must all be recut whenever a team changes boss.
cards.confusables: django-guardian — permissions are STORED rows that must be rewritten on reassignment; the chosen engine recomputes them from FKs.
cards.evidence_quote: they derive from current FKs, so nothing must be kept in sync on reassignment

cards.question: Why does ghost-crm's app map put `ExpenseClaim` in `accounting` and `LeaveApplication` in `hr` rather than give the docs' `personal` and `manager` modules their own Django apps?
cards.answer: Manager approves what personal requests, so two model apps would import each other. With the models in `hr` and `accounting`, `manager` and `personal` are only VIEW layers and no cycle exists. DESIGN TARGET.
cards.explanation: Bonus: approving a claim and creating its `Expense` stay inside one app, so the conversion is atomic. Payroll reaches accounting only through the `payroll_run_completed` signal; `hr` never imports accounting models.
cards.confusables: `personal` / `manager` apps with their own models — they would IMPORT each other; as view layers they own no models to import.
cards.evidence_quote: LeaveApplication lives in `hr`; ExpenseClaim lives in `accounting`

cards.question: ghost-crm: `npm run docs:dev` dies with `ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED`. What is the cause and what do you change?
cards.answer: Run on Node 14/16, or `export NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider` first. Cause: the lockfile pins webpack 4, which hashes with MD4; Node 17+ ships OpenSSL 3, which disables MD4.
cards.explanation: Install with `npm ci`, never `npm install`: the lockfile is `lockfileVersion` 1 and a modern npm rewrites it. The break is inferred from the pins; no live build was run when the skill was written.
cards.evidence_quote: Webpack 4 hashes with MD4 via `crypto.createHash('md4')`.

cards.question: ghost-crm: you must finish the Skhokho-to-Ghost-CRM rebrand. Why is a find-and-replace of `skhokho` across `docs/` forbidden, and what is the smallest safe procedure?
cards.answer: Verdict: rebrand ABOVE the References header only. (1) A blunt replace also rewrites the archived URLs inside the blocks, destroying the only route record. (2) Edit prose, the `config.js` title / description / nav and `package.json`; the progress metric is the body column of `audit_branding.py`, whose refs column must never move. (3) Keep a visible Skhokho origin statement: attribution may not be erased.
cards.explanation: `split_md()` in the audit cuts each page at the header, which is why body debt and archive are counted apart. Open direction (frontier F4): extend the rewrite-with-archive pattern to prose behind a dry-run default and anchor the block by header regex.
